update.title: tree: Avoid building a zero tree for poly_int coefficients
update.body:
On targets with NUM_POLY_INT_COEFFS > 1 (AArch64, RISC-V), converting an
INTEGER_CST to a poly_offset_int or poly_widest_int, as wi::to_poly_offset
and wi::to_poly_widest do, fills the trailing coefficients using
wi::ints_for<...>::zero.  For the tree-backed extended_tree types this
called build_zero_cst, which looks up the INTEGER_CST cache on every
conversion.

These conversions are frequent.  For example get_ref_base_and_extent
does them for every COMPONENT_REF, ARRAY_REF and MEM_REF it decomposes,
so the alias oracle pays for it on each statement visited by the alias
walkers.  In an AArch64 -O3 profile of a C++ file, wide_int_to_tree was
about 1% of the compiler's instructions as self cost, mostly reached
from get_ref_base_and_extent via refs_may_alias_p_2.

extended_tree has a fixed precision independent of the type of the tree,
so any zero INTEGER_CST represents the coefficient.  Return
integer_zero_node instead.  The unextended_tree variant takes its
precision from the type and is unchanged.

The test input is the C++ test suite of fmtlib/fmt
(https://github.com/fmtlib/fmt),
built with CMake in Release mode (-O3 -DNDEBUG -std=gnu++11).

instructions drop printf-test.cc -2.8%, format-test.cc
-1.5%, all 8 translation units combined -1.9%.

Bootstrapped and tested on aarch64-none-linux-gnu.

gcc/ChangeLog:

	* tree.h (wi::ints_for<generic_wide_int<extended_tree<N>>,
	INL_CONST_PRECISION>::zero): Return integer_zero_node.
	(wi::ints_for<generic_wide_int<extended_tree<N>>,
	CONST_PRECISION>::zero): Likewise.

Signed-off-by: Kyrylo Tkachov <ktkachov@nvidia.com>

update.title: RISC-V: Fix reg overlap for vs1 of vwadd[u].wv
update.body:
The vs2 of the vwadd[u].wv is read with EEW = 2 * SEW while the vs1
is read with EEW = SEW.  The section 5.2 of the vector spec reserves
any encoding in which one vector register supplies source operands
with two or more different EEWs.  Thus, the vs1 must not fall inside
the vs2 register group, but we may have below asm dump when the vs1
comes from the vs2 register group.

  vwadd.wv v4,v4,v6

Like the vfwadd.wv, take the Wn4 constraint for the operand 3 (aka vs2)
of the vwadd[u].wv.  See below issue of the riscv-isa-manual for more
details.

  https://github.com/riscv/riscv-isa-manual/issues/2350

gcc/ChangeLog:

	* config/riscv/vector.md: Take the Wn4 constraint for the
	operand 3 of the vwadd[u].wv.

update.title: RISC-V: Adjust vwadd[u].wv m4 test cases for reg overlap
update.body:
After the Wn4 constraint is taken for the operand 3 (aka vs2) of the
vwadd[u].wv, the register allocation of the m4 test cases changes
under high register pressure.  The vs1 still overlaps the highest part
of the vd and doesn't overlap the vs2 register group, which is the same
as the vfwadd.wv.

  vwadd.wv v16,v0,v20

Thus, adjust the asm check of these test cases.

gcc/testsuite/ChangeLog:

	* gcc.target/riscv/rvv/autovec/group_overlap/vwadd_wv-i8-m4.c: Adjust
	asm check.
